title: KCET 2023 Physics
subject: physics
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A3

questions.q: When a p-n junction diode is in forward bias, which type of charge carriers flows in the connecting wire?
questions.explanation: Inside the diode both holes and electrons carry current, but in the external connecting wire current is always carried by free electrons.

questions.q: A full-wave rectifier with diodes D$_1$ and D$_2$ is used to rectify 50 Hz alternating voltage. The diode D$_1$ conducts ____ times in one second.
questions.explanation: In a full-wave rectifier each diode conducts for one half-cycle every full cycle, so D$_1$ conducts once per cycle, i.e. 50 times per second for a 50 Hz supply.

questions.q: The truth table for the given circuit is [A and B feed a top gate that is XNOR (a curved-input gate with an output bubble) and a bottom gate that is XOR (curved-input gate, no bubble); both outputs feed a final NAND gate (AND-shape with output bubble) whose output is Y]
questions.explanation: XOR(A,B) and XNOR(A,B) are always complements of each other, so NAND of the two outputs is NOT(X·\overline{X}) = NOT(0) = 1 for every input combination, giving Y = 1 always, which is option B.

questions.q: The energy gap of an LED is 2.4 eV. When the LED is switched 'ON', the momentum of the emitted photons is
In the following equation representing $\beta^{-}$ decay, the number of neutrons in the nucleus X is $^{210}_{83}\text{Bi} \rightarrow X + e^{-1} + \bar{\nu}$
questions.explanation: In $\beta^-$ decay a neutron converts to a proton, so X has Z = 84, A = 210 (i.e. $^{210}_{84}$Po). Neutrons = A − Z = 210 − 84 = 126.

questions.q: A nucleus with mass number 220 initially at rest emits an alpha particle. If the Q value of the reaction is 5.5 MeV, calculate the value of kinetic energy of the alpha particle.
questions.explanation: By momentum conservation the alpha particle carries KE = Q×(A−4)/A = 5.5×216/220 = 5.4 MeV.

questions.q: A radioactive sample has half-life of 3 years. The time required for the activity of the sample to reduce to $\dfrac{1}{5}$th of its initial value is about

A body of mass 10 kg is kept on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the body and the surface is 0.5. A horizontal force of 60 N is applied on the body. The resulting acceleration of the body is about
questions.explanation: Friction force = μmg = 0.5×10×10 = 50 N. Net force = 60 − 50 = 10 N, so a = 10/10 = 1 ms$^{-2}$.

questions.q: A ball of mass 0.2 kg is thrown vertically down from a height of 10 m. It collides with the floor and loses 50% of its energy and then rises back to the same height. The value of its initial velocity is
questions.explanation: To rise back to 10 m the rebound speed must be $\sqrt{2gh}$ = 14.14 ms$^{-1}$, so KE just after collision = 100m. This is half the KE just before collision, so KE before = 200m, giving speed before impact v = 20 ms$^{-1}$. Using v$^2$ = u$^2$+2gh: 400 = u$^2$+200, so u ≈ 14 ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a rigid body about an axis
options: does not depend on its shape.
depends on the position of axis of rotation.
does not depend on its size.
does not depend on its mass.
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.explanation: Moment of inertia depends on the mass distribution relative to the chosen axis, so it changes with the position of the axis of rotation.

questions.q: Seven identical discs are arranged in a planar pattern, so as to touch each other as shown in the figure [six discs arranged in a ring, each touching its two neighbours and the seventh disc at the centre]. Each disc has mass 'm' radius R. What is the moment of inertia of system of six discs about an axis passing through the centre of central disc and normal to plane of all discs?
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.explanation: Each outer disc's centre is at distance 2R from the central axis, so by the parallel axis theorem each contributes $\frac{1}{2}mR^2+m(2R)^2=4.5mR^2$; for six discs this gives 27mR$^2$ (option D). KEA's key accepted both B and D for this version, so both are listed here, with D matching the exact calculation.

questions.q: The true length of a wire is 3.678 cm. When the length of this wire is measured using instrument A, the length of the wire is 3.5 cm. When the length of the wire is measured using instrument B, it is found to have length 3.38 cm. Then the
options: measurement with A is more accurate while measurement with B is more precise.
measurement with B is more accurate and precise.
measurement with A is more precise while measurement with B is more accurate.
measurement with A is more accurate and precise.
questions.explanation: A's reading (3.5 cm) is closer to the true value 3.678 cm, so A is more accurate; B's reading has more decimal places (finer resolution), so B is more precise.

questions.q: A body is moving along a straight line with initial velocity v$_0$. Its acceleration a is constant. After t seconds, its velocity becomes v. The average velocity of the body over the given time interval is
questions.explanation: Average velocity = (v+v$_0$)/2. Since at = v − v$_0$, $\dfrac{v^2-v_0^2}{2at}=\dfrac{(v-v_0)(v+v_0)}{2(v-v_0)}=\dfrac{v+v_0}{2}$, matching option C.

questions.q: A particle is in uniform circular motion. Related to one complete revolution of the particle, which among the statements is incorrect?
options: Displacement of the particle is zero.
Average speed of the particle is zero.
Average velocity of the particle is zero.
Average acceleration of the particle is zero.
questions.explanation: Average speed = distance travelled/time = circumference/T, which is nonzero; so the statement that average speed is zero is incorrect.

questions.q: 100 g of ice at 0 °C is mixed with 100 g of water at 100 °C. The final temperature of the mixture is [Take L$_f$ = 3.36 × 10$^5$ J kg$^{-1}$ and S$_w$ = 4.2 × 10$^3$ J kg$^{-1}$k$^{-1}$]

The P-V diagram of a Carnot's engine is shown in the graph below [P(kPa) vs V(cm$^3$): a cycle A$\to$B$\to$C$\to$D$\to$A with A at V=2.5, P=1600; B at V=3.75, P=1200; C at V=6.25, P=400; D at V$\approx$3, P=1000, joined in sequence tracing the cycle]. The engine uses 1 mole of an ideal gas as working substance. From the graph, the area enclosed by the P-V diagram is [The heat supplied to the gas is 8000 J]
questions.explanation: The P-axis is in kPa (not Pa), so the enclosed loop area (work done per cycle) comes out to 3000 J, consistent with the given 8000 J heat input giving a plausible cycle efficiency.

questions.q: When a planet revolves around the Sun, in general, for the planet
options: linear momentum and aerial velocity are constant.
kinetic and potential energy of the planet are constant.
angular momentum about the Sun and aerial velocity of the planet are constant.
linear momentum and linear velocity are constant.
questions.explanation: Since gravity is a central force, angular momentum about the Sun is conserved, and by Kepler's second law the areal velocity is constant.

questions.q: A stretched wire of a material whose Young's modulus Y = 2 × 10$^{11}$ Nm$^{-2}$ has Poisson's ratio 0.25. Its lateral strain $\varepsilon_l = 10^{-3}$. The elastic energy density of the wire is
questions.explanation: Longitudinal strain = lateral strain/Poisson's ratio = 10$^{-3}$/0.25 = 4×10$^{-3}$. Energy density = $\frac{1}{2}Y\varepsilon^2$ = 0.5×2×10$^{11}$×(4×10$^{-3}$)$^2$ = 1.6×10$^6$ Jm$^{-3}$.

questions.q: A closed water tank has cross-sectional area A. It has a small hole at a depth of h from the free surface of water [tank of pressure P$_0$ above the water, height H to the hole, hole of radius r at depth h from the surface]. The radius of the hole is r so that $r \ll \sqrt{A/\pi}$. If P$_0$ is the pressure inside the tank above water level, and P$_a$ is the atmospheric pressure, the rate of flow of the water coming out of the hole is [ρ is the density of water]
questions.explanation: By Bernoulli's theorem, the efflux speed is $v=\sqrt{2gh+2(P_0-P_a)/\rho}$, so the volume flow rate is $\pi r^2 v$.

questions.q: A positively charged glass rod is brought near uncharged metal sphere, which is mounted on an insulated stand. If the glass rod is removed, the net charge on the metal sphere is
questions.explanation: Bringing the rod near only redistributes charge on the sphere by induction; once the rod is removed with no contact, the sphere's net charge remains zero.

questions.q: In the situation shown in the diagram [a dipole with charge −Q at A and +Q at B, separated by 2a with midpoint O; a small charge −q is at point p directly above O at perpendicular distance r], magnitude of q $\ll$ |Q| and r $\gg$ a. The net force on the free charge −q and net torque on it about O at the instant shown are respectively [p = 2aQ is the dipole moment]
questions.explanation: At the equatorial point p (r $\gg$ a), the dipole field is $E=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{p}{r^3}$ antiparallel to $\vec p$; the force on the charge $-q$ is $\vec F=-q\vec E=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{pq}{r^3}\hat i$ (along $\vec p$). Taking torque about O, $\vec\tau=\vec r\times\vec F=(r\hat j)\times\left(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{pq}{r^3}\hat i\right)=-\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{pq}{r^2}\hat k$, matching option D.

questions.q: Pressure of ideal gas at constant volume is proportional to ____.
options: average potential energy of the molecules
average kinetic energy of the molecules
questions.explanation: From kinetic theory, PV = (2/3)E where E is the total translational kinetic energy of the gas molecules, so at constant V, P is proportional to the total energy of the gas.

questions.q: A block of mass m is connected to a light spring of force constant k. The system is placed inside a damping medium of damping constant b. The instantaneous values of displacement, acceleration and energy of the block are x, a and E respectively. The initial amplitude of oscillation is A and ω' is the angular frequency of oscillations. The incorrect expression related to the damped oscillations is
questions.explanation: The correct displacement equation for a damped oscillator is $x=Ae^{-\frac{bt}{2m}}\cos(\omega't+\phi)$; option D omits the time dependence and the factor 2 in the exponent, making it the incorrect expression.

questions.q: The speed of sound in an ideal gas at a given temperature T is v. The rms speed of gas molecules at that temperature is v$_{rms}$. The ratio of the velocities v and v$_{rms}$ for helium and oxygen gases are X and X' respectively. Then $\dfrac{X}{X'}$ is equal to

A uniform electric field vector $\vec E$ exists along horizontal direction as shown [field lines point rightward; a small charge q is slowly taken from point A along a curved (wavy) path to point B, where B is displaced horizontally by distance x from A]. The electric potential at A is V$_A$. A small point charge q is slowly taken from A to B along the curved path as shown. The potential energy of the charge when it is at point B is
questions.explanation: Since the field points from A towards B, the potential drops by Ex over that horizontal displacement, so V$_B$=V$_A$−Ex, giving potential energy U = q[V$_A$−Ex].

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance C$_1$ with a dielectric slab in between its plates is connected to a battery. It has a potential difference V$_1$ across its plates. When the dielectric slab is removed, keeping the capacitor connected to the battery, the new capacitance and potential difference are C$_2$ and V$_2$ respectively. Then,
questions.explanation: Since the capacitor stays connected to the battery, the potential difference is fixed by the battery (V$_1$=V$_2$); removing the dielectric decreases capacitance, so C$_1$>C$_2$.

questions.q: A cubical Gaussian surface has side of length a = 10 cm. Electric field lines are parallel to x-axis as shown [cube with faces ABCD and EFGH normal to the x-axis]. The magnitudes of electric fields through surfaces ABCD and EFGH are 6kNC$^{-1}$ and 9kNC$^{-1}$ respectively. Then the total charge enclosed by the cube is [Take $\varepsilon_0=9\times10^{-12}$ Fm$^{-1}$]
questions.explanation: Net flux = (E$_2$−E$_1$)a$^2$ = (9000−6000)×(0.1)$^2$ = 30 Nm$^2$/C. Charge enclosed Q = $\varepsilon_0\times$flux = 9×10$^{-12}\times$30 = 0.27 nC.

questions.q: Electric field at a distance 'r' from an infinitely long uniformly charged straight conductor, having linear charge density $\lambda$ is E$_1$. Another uniformly charged conductor having same linear charge density $\lambda$ is bent into a semicircle of radius 'r'. The electric field at its centre is E$_2$. Then
questions.explanation: Field at centre of a uniformly charged semicircular arc of radius r is $2k\lambda/r$, which is the same as the field of an infinite line charge at distance r, so E$_1$=E$_2$.

questions.q: Five capacitors each of value 1 μF are connected as shown in the figure [two 1μF capacitors in series from A form the top and bottom arms of a bridge, one 1μF capacitor bridges the midpoints, and two more 1μF capacitors in series form the arms leading to B, symmetric about the bridging capacitor]. The equivalent capacitance between A and B is
questions.explanation: By symmetry of the balanced bridge network, no charge flows through the bridging capacitor, and the two series-parallel branches (each two 1 μF capacitors in series, giving 0.5 μF, in parallel with each other) combine to give an equivalent capacitance of 1 μF between A and B.

questions.q: For a given electric current the drift velocity of conduction electrons in a copper wire is v$_d$ and their mobility is μ. When the current is increased at constant temperature
options: v$_d$ remains the same, μ increases
v$_d$ decreases, μ remains the same
v$_d$ remains the same, μ decreases
v$_d$ increases, μ remains the same
questions.explanation: I = nAev$_d$, so increasing current increases v$_d$ proportionally; mobility μ = v$_d$/E depends on the relaxation time (hence temperature) and stays unchanged at constant temperature.

questions.q: Ten identical cells each emf 2 V and internal resistance 1 Ω are connected in series with two cells wrongly connected. A resistor of 10 Ω is connected to the combination. What is the current through the resistor?
questions.explanation: Net emf = (10−2×2)×2 = 12 V, total internal resistance = 10×1 = 10 Ω. Current = 12/(10+10) = 0.6 A.

questions.q: The equivalent resistance between the points A and B in the following circuit is [a ladder network: A connects through three 2Ω resistors in series along the top (open at the far end), B connects through three 2Ω resistors in series along the bottom (open at the far end), with three 2Ω resistors as vertical rungs joining the top and bottom rails at each junction]
questions.explanation: Reducing from the open (right) end: the rightmost rung (2Ω) in series with the top and bottom 2Ω segments (2+2Ω) forms a 6Ω path in parallel with the middle rung's 2Ω, giving 1.5Ω; that combines with the next 2Ω top+bottom segments (2+2Ω) to form a 5.5Ω path in parallel with the left rung's 2Ω, giving 22/15Ω; adding the outer 2Ω top and bottom segments gives 2+22/15+2 = 82/15 ≈ 5.5 Ω between A and B.

questions.q: A charged particle is subjected to acceleration in a cyclotron as shown [two D-shaped dees D$_1$, D$_2$ with an oscillator RFO connected across the gap, magnetic field $\vec B$ into the plane, particle spiralling outward]. The charged particle undergoes increase in its speed
options: Inside D$_1$, D$_2$ and the gaps
Only in the gap between D$_1$ and D$_2$
questions.explanation: Inside the dees there is only a magnetic field, which changes direction of velocity but not speed; the particle is accelerated (speed increases) only by the electric field in the gap between the dees.

questions.q: The resistance of a carbon resistor is 4.7 kΩ ± 5%. The colour of the third band is
questions.explanation: 4.7 kΩ = 47×10$^2$ Ω: yellow(4)-violet(7)-red(×10$^2$, third band)-gold(±5%).

questions.q: The four bands of a colour coded resistor are of the colours gray, red, gold and gold. The value of the resistance of the resistor is
questions.explanation: gray=8, red=2, gold (third band, multiplier) = ×0.1, gold (fourth band) = ±5% tolerance, giving 82×0.1 = 8.2Ω ± 5%.

questions.q: A wire of resistance R is connected across a cell of emf $\varepsilon$ and internal resistance r. The current through the circuit is I. In time t, the work done by the battery to establish the current I is
questions.explanation: Work done by the emf source in time t is W = $\varepsilon$It, part of which is dissipated in R and part in the internal resistance r.

questions.q: The Curie temperatures of Cobalt and iron are 1400 K and 1000 K respectively. At T = 1600 K, the ratio of magnetic susceptibility of Cobalt to that of iron is
The torque acting on a magnetic dipole placed in uniform magnetic field is zero, when the angle between the dipole axis and the magnetic field is ____.
questions.explanation: Torque $\tau=mB\sin\theta$ is zero when $\theta=0\degree$ (dipole aligned with field), i.e. the angle itself is zero.

questions.q: The horizontal component of Earth's magnetic field at a place is 3 × 10$^{-5}$ T. If the dip at that place is 45°, the resultant magnetic field at that place is
A proton and an alpha-particle moving with the same velocity enter a uniform magnetic field with their velocities perpendicular to the magnetic field. The ratio of radii of their circular paths is

A moving coil galvanometer is converted into an ammeter of range 0 to 5 mA. The galvanometer resistance is 90 Ω and the shunt resistance has a value of 10 Ω. If there are 50 divisions in the galvanometer-turned-ammeter on either sides of zero, its current sensitivity is
questions.explanation: By the shunt condition I$_g$R$_g$=(I−I$_g$)R$_s$: 90I$_g$=(5mA−I$_g$)10, giving I$_g$=0.5 mA for full-scale (50 divisions). Sensitivity = 50/0.5mA = 1×10$^5$ div/A.

questions.q: A positively charged particle of mass m is passed through a velocity selector. It moves horizontally rightward without deviation along the line $y=\dfrac{2mv}{qB}$ with a speed v. The electric field is vertically downwards and the magnetic field is into the plane of the paper. Now, the electric field is switched off at t = 0. The angular momentum of the charged particle about origin O at $t=\dfrac{\pi m}{qB}$ is [figure: axes with the particle's line of motion at height $y_0=2mv/(qB)$ above O, $\vec v$ rightward, $\vec E$ downward, $\vec B$ into the page]
questions.explanation: With E off, the particle moves in a circle of radius r=mv/(qB) under B alone. Direct calculation of L about O at t=πm/(qB) (half a revolution) gives 4m²v²/(qB) = 4m²E²/(qB³), which does not exactly match any option; KEA awarded a grace mark for this question in this version, so option D (the standard-form answer closest to this type of problem) is kept here as the best estimate.

questions.q: In series LCR circuit at resonance, the phase difference between voltage and current is
questions.explanation: At resonance the impedance of a series LCR circuit is purely resistive, so voltage and current are in phase (phase difference zero).

questions.q: An ideal transformer has a turns ratio of 10. When the primary is connected to 220 V, 50 Hz ac source, the power output is
questions.explanation: An ideal transformer has no power loss, so the output power always equals the input power regardless of the turns ratio.

questions.q: The current in a coil changes from 2A to 5A in 0.3s. The magnitude of emf induced in the coil is 1.0 V. The value of self-inductance of the coil is

A metallic rod of length 1 m held along east-west direction is allowed to fall down freely. Given horizontal component of earth's magnetic field B$_H$ = 3 × 10$^{-5}$ T. The emf induced in the rod at an instant t = 2s after it is released is (Take g = 10 ms$^{-2}$)

A square loop of side 2 cm enters a magnetic field with a constant speed of 2 cm s$^{-1}$ as shown [square loop of side 2 cm moving right with speed 2 cm/s into a field region of width 10 cm, B=0.5 T into the page]. The front edge enters the field at t = 0s. Which of the following graph correctly depicts the induced emf in the loop? (Take clockwise direction positive)
options: Triangular rise to 2×10$^{-4}$ V from t=0 to 1s, zero from 1 to 5s, negative triangular dip from 5 to 6s
Negative triangular dip from t=0 to 1s, zero from 1 to 5s, positive triangular rise to 2×10$^{-4}$ V from 5 to 6s
Constant −2×10$^{-4}$ V step from t=0 to 1s, zero from 1 to 5s, constant +2×10$^{-4}$ V step from 5 to 6s
Constant +2×10$^{-4}$ V step from t=0 to 1s, zero from 1 to 5s, constant −2×10$^{-4}$ V step from 5 to 6s
questions.explanation: While entering (0 to 1s) and leaving (5 to 6s) the field, a constant emf of magnitude Blv = 0.5×0.02×0.02 = 2×10$^{-4}$ V is induced with opposite signs, and it is zero while the loop is fully inside the field (1 to 5s), matching option C.

questions.q: For a given pair of transparent media, the critical angle for which colour is maximum?
questions.explanation: Critical angle $\theta_c=\sin^{-1}(1/n)$ is largest for the smallest refractive index; red light has the least refractive index among visible colours, so it has the maximum critical angle.

questions.q: An equiconvex lens made of glass of refractive index $\dfrac{3}{2}$ has focal length f in air. It is completely immersed in water of refractive index $\dfrac{4}{3}$. The percentage change in the focal length is
questions.explanation: 1/f $\propto (n_{lens}/n_{medium}-1)$. In air this factor is (3/2−1)=0.5; in water it is ((3/2)/(4/3)−1)=1/8, i.e. 1/4 as large, so f becomes 4 times larger — a 300% increase.

questions.q: A point object is moving at a constant speed of 1 ms$^{-1}$ along the principal axis of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The speed of the image is also 1 ms$^{-1}$, when the object is at ____ cm from the optic centre of the lens.
questions.explanation: Image speed equals object speed when magnification magnitude is 1, which for a convex lens occurs when the object is at u=2f=20 cm (real, inverted, same-size image).

questions.q: When light propagates through a given homogeneous medium, the velocities of
options: primary wavefronts are lesser than those of secondary wavelets.
primary wavefronts are greater than or equal to those of secondary wavelets.
primary wavefront and wavelets are equal.
primary wavefront are larger than those of secondary wavelets.
questions.explanation: In a homogeneous medium the speed of light is the same everywhere, so the primary wavefront and Huygens' secondary wavelets travel with equal speed.

questions.q: Total impedance of a series LCR circuit varies with angular frequency of the AC source connected to it as shown in the graph [Z vs ω curve, minimum Z$_{min}$ near ω=500 rad/s, with Z=√2 Z$_{min}$ at ω=400 and ω=600 rad/s]. The quality factor Q of the series LCR circuit is
questions.explanation: The bandwidth is $\Delta\omega$ = 600−400 = 200 rad/s at resonance $\omega_0$=500 rad/s, so Q = $\omega_0/\Delta\omega$ = 500/200 = 2.5.

questions.q: The ratio of the magnitudes of electric field to the magnetic field of an electromagnetic wave is of the order of
questions.explanation: For an EM wave, E/B = c ≈ 3×10$^8$ ms$^{-1}$, of the order 10$^8$ ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: For a point object, which of the following always produces virtual image in air?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, diminished, erect image for a real object placed at any distance; lenses and concave mirrors can form real images depending on object position.

questions.q: In an experiment to study photo-electric effect the observed variation of stopping potential with frequency of incident radiation is as shown in the figure [straight line graph of stopping potential V$_0$ vs frequency $\nu$, cutting the frequency axis at $\nu_0$ and rising linearly beyond it]. The slope and y-intercept respectively are
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.explanation: From eV$_0$=h\nu−φ, V$_0$=(h/e)υ−φ/e; slope = h/e, and since V$_0$=0 at υ=υ$_0$, the y-intercept (extrapolated to υ=0) is −hυ$_0$/e.

questions.q: In the Rutherford's alpha scattering experiment, as the impact parameter increases, the scattering angle of the alpha particle
questions.explanation: A larger impact parameter means the alpha particle passes farther from the nucleus, experiencing weaker repulsion and hence smaller deflection (scattering angle decreases).

questions.q: Three energy levels of hydrogen atom and the corresponding wavelength of the emitted radiation due to different electron transition are as shown [E$_3$ at top, E$_2$ middle, E$_1$ bottom; $\lambda_3$ is the E$_3\to$E$_2$ transition, $\lambda_1$ is the E$_2\to$E$_1$ transition, $\lambda_2$ is the direct E$_3\to$E$_1$ transition]. Then
questions.explanation: Energy conservation: (E$_3$−E$_1$) = (E$_3$−E$_2$)+(E$_2$−E$_1$), i.e. hc/λ$_2$ = hc/λ$_3$+hc/λ$_1$, giving $\lambda_2=\lambda_1\lambda_3/(\lambda_1+\lambda_3)$.

questions.q: An unpolarised light of intensity I is passed through two polaroids kept one after the other with their planes parallel to each other. The intensity of light emerging from second polaroid is $\dfrac{I}{4}$. The angle between the pass axes of the polaroids is
questions.explanation: The first polaroid halves the intensity to I/2; applying Malus's law, (I/2)cos²θ = I/4 gives cos²θ = 1/2, so θ = 45°.

questions.q: In the Young's double slit experiment, the intensity of light passing through each of the two double slits is 2 × 10$^{-2}$ Wm$^{-2}$. The screen-slit distance is very large in comparison with slit-slit distance. The fringe width is $\beta$. The distance between the central maximum and a point P on the screen is $x=\dfrac{\beta}{3}$. Then the total light intensity at that point is
questions.explanation: Path difference x=β/3 corresponds to phase $\delta=2\pi/3$. I = 4I$_0$cos²(δ/2) = 4×2×10$^{-2}$×cos²(60°) = 4×2×10$^{-2}\times0.25$ = 2×10$^{-2}$ Wm$^{-2}$.

questions.q: A 60 W source emits monochromatic light of wavelength 662.5 nm. The number of photons emitted per second is
